Maths at work

Health and science

Jobs in this route, and the maths they use.

Ratio

Hospital nurse

Route: Health and science

Liquid medicine comes at a strength, such as 250 mg in 5 ml. Nurses use: volume = what you want ÷ what you have × what it is in. The prescription is 125 mg. The bottle says 250 mg in 5 ml.

  1. \(125 \div 250 = 0.5\).
  2. \(0.5 \times 5 = 2.5\) ml.

Averages and statistics

Practice nurse

Route: Health and science

Uses example figures: the numbers marked (example figure) or (example figures) are made up to show the method.

One blood pressure reading can mislead, so NICE says to take readings at home, twice a day for 4 to 7 days, ignore the first day, and use the mean of the rest. After day 1, the top (systolic) numbers are 138, 134, 136, 140, 132, 136 (example figures).

  1. Add them: 816.
  2. Mean: \(816 \div 6 = 136\).
  3. The doctor compares that average, with the clinic reading, against NICE's limits.

Health visitor

Route: Health and science

Babies' weights are plotted on growth charts with centile lines. A centile shows how many healthy children are expected to be below that line. A baby is on the 91st centile.

  1. 91 out of 100 healthy babies the same age are expected to weigh less.
  2. \(100 - 91 = 9\) out of 100 are expected to weigh more.

Sources

Every job and every figure that is not an example comes from a public page you can check.

  • Hospital nurse: Royal College of Nursing, "Safety in numbers: dosage for liquid medicines"
  • Practice nurse: NICE guideline NG136, Hypertension in adults
  • Health visitor: Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health, UK-WHO growth charts
